messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] 22:04 UTC - eu-west2 hot-shard saturation causing elevated 503s for Dedicated pools. Incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026-21987 @channel

liza: Oncall. Seeing one GPU shard in eu-west2 hit sustained queue depth and kernel timeouts. Traffic piling up and triggering client retries.

rob: Confirmed high tail latencies on shard g-shard-7f. Background rebalance stalled due to IO pressure.

nate: Mitigation options: 1) mark shard as degraded and reroute to backup pool 2) drain shard and reprovision 3) temporarily enable tenant-level fallback to cross-region. Proposing 1+3 now.

infra-runner: Applied routing tag to divert non-SLA traffic from g-shard-7f -> eu-west2-backup. Command: apply-route --from g-shard-7f --tag fallback=backup.

ops-bot: Update 22:12 UTC - diversion active. Non-SLA traffic diverted ~40%. 503s down ~48%. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/d/ingress/eu-west2-hot-shard

liza: Starting drain of g-shard-7f. Will cordon pod set and spin new nodes with tuned io-scheduler.

rob: While draining, noticed repeated large-sequence requests from tenant T-42 that bypassed batching and caused KV-cache churn. Reaching out to account team.

cs-ops: Notified customer owners for T-42 and opened ticket. Advising retry/backoff.

infra-runner: New nodes provisioned with io limits and kernel patches. Reprovision complete; draining complete at 22:38 UTC.

ops-bot: Update 22:41 UTC - degraded shard removed; majority traffic restored. Monitoring for 30m. Postmortem placeholder: https://docs.redwood.ai/postmortems/INC-2026-21987

liza: Next steps: 1) full RCA kickoff tomorrow 2) add automated detection for hot-shard IO growth patterns 3) consider tenant soft-limits on long-sequence unbatched requests.

rob: Quick remediation note: adding a short-term per-tenant slow-path to limit concurrent long-sequence calls until detection lands. cfg id: slowpath-21987.

ops-bot: Final update 22:50 UTC - Incident mitigated. If you see regressions re-open thread. :white_check_mark:
